pr_body:
Interactive development of UI features requires a few prerequisites to
be built to satisfy editor requirements. Specifically, cluster-ui
depends on the typings produced from building
@cockroachlabs/crdb-protobuf-client, db-console depends on the typings
produced from building both the protobuf client and cluster-ui, and
eslint editor plugins require @cockroachlabs/eslint-plugin-crdb to be
compiled and the compiled output to be in the Bazel workspace. Add a
./dev generate js target that compiles the minimum set of dependencies
to bootstrap a development environment.

This requires a small change to the `tsconfig.json` for cluster-ui and
db-console to ensure they know where to find the Bazel-produced output
of the packages in this repo.

fixes #84738

issue_context.title: dev: should provide `dev generate js` to copy generated JS code into the workspace
issue_context.body:
See [internal discussion](https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/C019A8NANH0/p1658335821065579).

Epic CRDB-8349

Jira issue: CRDB-17837

review_comments: Looks like `dev generate js` doesn't call into `copyBuildOutputToWorkspace` and just does a `CopyAll`. Is that right? Is there any particular reason why it is not necessary here?

It is right!  The original idea was to use `copyBuildOutputToWorkspace()` to copy all of the compiled typings back into the bazel workspace, but that'd require someone to rerun `./dev generate js` after every build for their IDE to see those changes.  That's a pretty tall order to ask of folks, so I made all of the TypeScript IDE tooling look in `_bazel/bin/…` for `.d.ts` files in addition to the normal `./node_modules/` location.  This allows a `./dev build` to produce new typings and for IDEs to pick them up immediately.  The only thing that did need to get copied into the workspace is a custom plugin for the JS linter: it has to be compiled before it can be used, and `eslint` doesn't seem to expose a configuration option to expand the search locations for plugins beyond the normal `node_modules` patterns.
